problem.title: B2B outreach is fast to get wrong.
problem.p1: Finding relevant businesses by hand is slow. Spreadsheets, manual searches, copy-paste between tools.
problem.p2: Cold outreach without controls burns sender reputation, triggers complaints, and gets domains blocked.
problem.p3: Teams need source attribution per lead, a review gate before any message goes out, and clear suppression handling.
problem.p4: And someone has to remember to verify the sending domain, configure SMTP, and stop campaigns when bounce rates rise.

solution.title: Collect, analyze, draft, review, send — in that order.
steps: Find websites from safe sources (OpenStreetMap, your CSV, or a paid search provider).
Crawl public pages politely (robots.txt, crawl-delay, custom user-agent).
Extract publicly visible business emails. Skip private areas and login pages.
Analyze each website: industry, offering, possible needs, confidence score.
Generate a personalized draft using only facts found on the site.
Review and approve manually with a compliance checkbox.
Send only after SMTP is ready, the sending domain is verified, and contact is activated.

safety.title: Hard gates between collection and sending.
items: Spam is strictly prohibited — confirmed or niche base only.
No automatic sending. Default approval required.
Drafts stay in pending_review until an operator confirms.
Unsubscribe and suppression enforced at every layer.
Sending domain must be verified before any campaign schedules.

Tenant-level limits and risk events visible to administrators.
Every lead carries its source URL, discovery time, and context snippet.
No private data, no leaked databases, no CAPTCHA bypass.

why.title: Different from generic outreach blasters.
items: The Collector module never sends. By design — it has no SMTP code at all.
A review gate sits between discovery and any outgoing message.
Every lead carries the source URL it came from. You can defend the list.
Imported contacts land in 'pending'. They never auto-activate to 'subscribed'.
Suppression and unsubscribe events flip future links and sends off.
Sending requires a verified domain, ready SMTP, and an activated contact.
No uncontrolled bulk: per-tenant caps, per-day caps, scheduler back-pressure.

antiSpam.title: Spam is strictly prohibited.
antiSpam.sub: This platform is built for legitimate B2B outreach only. Every send must go to a consented or niche-confirmed contact base.

rules.p: You may send only to your own opt-in contact base — people who gave you their email directly or through a confirmed sign-up.
Alternatively, use our platform's verified B2B base: publicly listed business contacts from Google Maps and public directories, segmented by industry niche.
Our base is divided by industry: cleaning services, dental clinics, beauty salons, auto repair, legal, HVAC, real estate, and more. You target a niche — not a mailbox dump.
Every outgoing email carries an unsubscribe link. A click removes the contact globally — no re-adds, no workarounds, enforced at platform level.
Sending to purchased lists, leaked data dumps, private scraped data, or any non-public source is forbidden and will result in immediate account suspension.
Spam complaints, excessive bounces, or complaint rates above threshold automatically suspend the tenant. All outreach activity is audited.

seo.title: Features — Email Platform
seo.description: Every module in the Email Platform: lead collector, website analyzer, outreach drafts, domain verification, sending controls, and safety gates.

features.title: Every module, explained.
features.sub: Email Platform is an operator console for B2B outreach. Below is every module in the platform — what it does, how it fits into the pipeline, and what it requires before it activates.

modules.p: The Collector finds public business websites from multiple sources: OpenStreetMap (free), Tavily search API, or user-uploaded CSV archives. It queues each source for crawling, deduplicates by domain across the tenant, and stores discovered contacts with their source URL and extraction context.
details: Perpetual mode runs automatically in the background, processing queued sources on a schedule.
Per-day source caps protect against accidental runaway crawls.
Each discovered contact carries the exact source URL, page snippet, and timestamp.
Respects robots.txt and crawl-delay headers. Never touches login or private pages.

modules.p: The Warehouse stores every collected company and contact. It shows industry classification, fit scoring, duplicate status, and all contact points per company. Leads can be filtered, searched, exported, or promoted to the Contacts module for outreach.
details: Industry classification: automatically applied via LLM-based classifier.
Product fit scoring: good_fit / weak_fit / not_fit per company profile.
Full source attribution on every contact.
CSV export available. Contacts promoted to Contacts module arrive as 'pending'.

modules.p: For each collected company website, the Analyzer fetches public pages and generates a structured profile: industry, offering description, possible pain points, confidence score, and detected language. This profile feeds the draft generator.
details: Analyzes publicly reachable pages only — no login bypass.
Confidence score 0–100 indicates how well the site content was understood.
Language detection for multilingual outreach targeting.
Analysis results are stored and re-used for draft generation.

modules.p: After website analysis, the generator produces a personalized outreach draft using only verified facts from the analyzed site. Drafts are addressed to the collected contact, reference real details from the website, and wait in 'pending_review' until an operator manually approves.
details: Uses only facts found on the analyzed website. No invented claims.
Draft includes subject line, body, and source attribution.
Status: pending_review → approved / rejected. Full audit trail.
Test-send available before campaign scheduling. Full send requires domain verified + SMTP ready.

modules.p: The Contacts module stores all addressable recipients. Contacts arrive as 'pending' — they never auto-activate. An operator must explicitly set them to 'subscribed' before any send is possible. Unsubscribe and bounce events flip status permanently.
details: Statuses: pending → subscribed / unsubscribed / bounced / complained.
No automatic transitions from pending to subscribed.
Suppression list checked before every outgoing message.
Global unsubscribes enforced across all tenants.

modules.p: Campaigns target a contact list and schedule outbound messages. They cannot be scheduled unless the sending domain is DNS-verified and SMTP reports 'ready'. Per-day caps, bounce monitoring, and complaint-rate thresholds apply automatically.
details: Requires: sending domain verified, SMTP ready, contact list with subscribed contacts.
Daily send limits enforced per tenant.
Auto-pause on bounce rate > 2% or complaint rate > 0.08%.
Tracking: open pixel, click redirect, unsubscribe endpoint — all per-message signed tokens.

modules.p: Before any campaign can run, the sending domain must pass DNS verification: SPF, DKIM (RSA 2048, auto-generated keypair), DMARC, and Return-Path CNAME. The platform generates the exact records to publish and re-checks on demand.
details: Auto-generates RSA 2048 DKIM keypair per domain.
Shows exact DNS records (value + type) to copy into your registrar.
Live DNS verification via Node.js dns module.
Domain status: pending → verified / failed / warning.

modules.p: Branded short links with click tracking, suppression-aware redirects, and tenant safety controls. Links can be inserted in outreach drafts or shared independently. Clicks are logged with timestamp and source.
details: Short URL with custom slug or auto-generated token.
Redirect target checked against suppression list.
Click events logged: timestamp, user-agent, IP (anonymized).
Per-link expiry and click caps available.

modules.p: Plan management, invoice history, trial period display, and manual payment confirmation flow. The billing UI is ready; a payment processor integration (Stripe, LiqPay, etc.) can be wired by the operator.
details: Plan tiers configurable by admin.
Trial period tracked from tenant creation.
Manual payment flow: contact admin with invoice number.
Suspension enforced when payment lapses.

modules.p: Super-admin view of every tenant: SMTP status, sending domains, active collectors, outreach volume, audit logs, and tenant-level kill switches. Used to onboard new tenants, set global defaults, and monitor platform health.
details: Create / suspend / delete tenants.
Override per-tenant safety settings.
View all collector jobs and outreach activity.
Global suppression list management.

modules.p: Each operator can update their display name, preferred language (EN/RU/UK), and change their password with current-password verification. Session management and logout.
details: Profile: full name, locale preference.
Password change: requires current password (Argon2id verified server-side).
Logout clears session and redirects to login.
Account info: email (read-only), role badge.

seo.title: How it works — Email Platform
seo.description: Step-by-step workflow: from source discovery to verified send. Every safety gate explained.

howItWorks.title: From source to reviewed message — every step.
howItWorks.sub: The platform enforces a linear pipeline. You cannot skip steps. Each gate requires the previous stage to complete successfully.
howItWorks.diagramAlt: Pipeline: Collector → Warehouse → Analyzer → Draft → Review → Test → Campaign

steps.p: Paste a website URL, upload a CSV of domains, run an OpenStreetMap search by category and city, or use the Tavily search provider. Each source becomes a Collector entry. Duplicate domains per tenant are skipped automatically.

The perpetual collector picks up queued sources on a schedule. It fetches public pages, extracts publicly listed business emails, and stores each contact with the source URL and page snippet. No login pages, no CAPTCHAs, no private areas.

Collected contacts are stored in the Lead Warehouse with status 'discovered'. Each contact has: source URL, discovery date, raw page snippet, company domain. No contact is addressable yet — they are warehouse-only.

Trigger website analysis on any warehouse company. The analyzer reads public pages and generates a structured profile: industry, offering, pain points (inferred from site content), confidence score, language. This profile is required for draft generation.
steps.gate: Requires: website must be publicly reachable.

steps.p: With an analysis on file, generate a personalized outreach draft. The generator uses only the analyzed website facts — no invented claims. Draft contains subject line, body, and full source attribution. Status: pending_review.
steps.gate: Requires: website analysis completed with confidence > 20.

steps.p: Every draft sits in pending_review until you open it, read it, and manually approve. The approval form shows the full draft, the analysis that generated it, the source contact, and a compliance checkbox. Reject with a reason. Full audit trail.
steps.gate: GATE: No draft can move to 'approved' without manual operator action.

steps.p: Before scheduling a campaign, use the test-send to deliver the approved draft to your own inbox. This verifies SMTP is working, the template renders correctly, and the unsubscribe link is reachable.
steps.gate: Requires: draft approved, SMTP configured and reachable, test email address set.

steps.p: Navigate to Domains and add your sending domain (e.g. mail.yourdomain.com). The platform generates SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and Return-Path records. Publish them at your DNS provider, then click Verify. Status must reach 'verified' before campaigns can run.
Set SMTP credentials in your environment or settings. The worker validates connectivity and auth on startup and before every campaign run. SMTP status must reach 'ready'.

Warehouse contacts promoted to the Contacts module arrive as 'pending'. Manually set each contact to 'subscribed' after verifying they are appropriate recipients. Pending contacts cannot receive campaigns.
steps.gate: GATE: Only subscribed contacts receive campaign messages.

steps.p: With all gates satisfied, create a campaign: choose list, select approved drafts, set schedule. The worker sends within daily limits, checks suppression before each message, tracks opens, clicks, bounces, and unsubscribes in real time. Campaign pauses automatically if bounce or complaint thresholds are reached.
steps.gate: All gates must pass: domain verified + SMTP ready + contacts subscribed + drafts approved.

seo.title: Operator Instructions — Email Platform
seo.description: Full operator manual. How to use every module: collector, warehouse, analysis, drafts, campaigns, domains, billing, and admin controls.

instructions.title: How to use every module.
instructions.sub: This guide covers every module in order of the pipeline. Read from top to bottom for a first setup; jump to any section for reference.

items.a: Navigate to /login. Enter your operator email and password. On success you land on /dashboard. Session is stored in an HttpOnly cookie (JWT, 24h). If the token expires, you are redirected to /login automatically.
Follow the setup wizard at /onboarding: (1) add a sending domain, (2) configure SMTP, (3) add your first source, (4) review your first draft, (5) send a test email.
Click the language flag in the top-right of any page. Available: EN / RU / UK. Preference is stored in a cookie and applies immediately without page reload.
Go to /collector. Click 'Add source'. Paste a URL (e.g. https://example.com). The source queues for crawling. The perpetual worker picks it up within the next cycle (up to 50 seconds).
In the Collector, click 'OSM search'. Enter a category (e.g. 'dental clinic'), a city or bounding box, and click Search. Matching business websites are imported as sources automatically.
Configure TAVILY_API_KEY in your .env file. Then use 'Search provider' in the Collector to run keyword queries. Results are deduped against existing sources.
Prepare a CSV with a 'url' column (and optionally 'label'). Upload in the Collector. Each row becomes a source. Duplicates are skipped.

The Stats page (/stats) shows today's crawl count, new leads found, analysis run, and draft generated. The Collector page shows each source with status: pending / queued / crawling / succeeded / failed / skipped.
Go to /warehouse. Companies and contacts are listed with industry, fit score, source, and discovery date. Use filters (industry, fit category, status) to narrow results.
Filter to the leads you want, then click Export CSV. The export includes company name, domain, email, source URL, industry, and fit score.
Select a lead (or use bulk select) and click 'Add to contacts'. The contact is created in the Contacts module with status 'pending'. You must manually activate them before they can receive campaigns.
From Admin, call GET /api/admin/warehouse/reclassify. This re-runs industry classification on all unclassified companies. Progress is visible in the API logs.
From the Warehouse, open a company record and click 'Analyze website'. The worker fetches public pages, runs the analysis, and stores the result. Takes 5–30 seconds depending on site complexity.
Industry classification, offering summary (2–3 sentences), possible pain points (inferred from site content), confidence score (0–100), and detected language.

A score below 30 means the site had too little usable content (e.g. one-pager, blocked JS-only site, or landing page under construction). Drafts generated from low-confidence analyses are marked accordingly.
From the Outreach page (/outreach), select a company with a completed analysis and click 'Generate draft'. The draft appears with status 'pending_review'.

Open the draft. Read the full message. Check that it references real, accurate facts from the website. Tick the compliance checkbox ('This message is accurate and compliant'). Click Approve. The draft status moves to 'approved'.
Click Reject and enter a reason. The draft is archived. You can regenerate from the company record.
With draft approved, click 'Send test'. Enter your test email address. The worker sends immediately via the configured SMTP. Check your inbox to verify delivery, formatting, and unsubscribe link.
Go to /campaigns. Click 'New campaign'. Enter name, subject, choose sender identity, and select a contact list. Set a schedule (immediately or specific date/time). Click Create.

A campaign cannot be scheduled until: (1) sending domain is DNS-verified, (2) SMTP status is 'ready', (3) the selected list has at least one 'subscribed' contact, (4) the campaign has at least one approved draft or template attached.
The Campaign detail page shows: sent, opened (unique), clicked (unique), bounced, unsubscribed, complained. Refreshes automatically. Campaign pauses if bounce rate > 2% or complaint rate > 0.08%.
Click Pause to stop sending (resumable). Click Cancel to stop permanently. In-flight messages already queued in Redis will complete.
Go to /domains. Click 'Add domain'. Enter the domain (use a subdomain like mail.yourdomain.com — not your root domain). The platform auto-generates a DKIM RSA 2048 keypair.
The Domains page shows four records: SPF (TXT), DKIM (TXT), DMARC (TXT on _dmarc.subdomain), and Return-Path (CNAME on bounce.subdomain). Publish all four at your DNS registrar or Cloudflare.
After publishing records, click 'Verify DNS' on the domain. The platform checks all four records live. Status moves to 'verified' when all four pass. DNS propagation can take up to 24 hours.
Expand 'Last verification detail' to see which records passed and which failed. Common issues: SPF record on wrong subdomain, DKIM TXT record truncated by DNS provider, CNAME pointing to wrong value.
Open the contact record. Click 'Activate' to change status from 'pending' to 'subscribed'. This is a manual action that indicates you have verified the contact is an appropriate recipient.
Select multiple contacts using the checkboxes. Click 'Bulk actions → Set subscribed'. A confirmation dialog shows the count before proceeding.

Unsubscribed contacts are flagged permanently. They cannot be re-subscribed via bulk actions. The suppression check before each send enforces this. If a contact unsubscribed, they will not receive messages even if accidentally added to a list.
Go to Contacts → Import CSV. Upload a file with columns: email (required), first_name, last_name, tags. All imported contacts arrive as 'pending'.
Go to /settings. Update your display name and preferred language. Click Save profile. Changes apply immediately.

In /settings, expand the password section. Enter your current password, new password (min 8 characters), and confirmation. Click Save password. The API verifies your current password (Argon2id) before accepting the change.
Click the logout button in Settings or the sidebar footer. The session cookie is cleared and you are redirected to /login.
Only accounts with the 'super_admin' role can access /admin. The sidebar shows the Admin link only to super-admins.
Admin → Tenants: view all tenants, create new tenants, suspend/reactivate, view their SMTP status and sending domain status.
Admin → Suppressions: view and manage the global suppression list. Emails on this list are blocked from receiving messages from any tenant.
Admin → Theme: set the platform-wide default theme (applies to new users and public pages). Individual operators can override in /settings.

seo.title: Safety & Anti-Abuse — Email Platform
seo.description: How Email Platform prevents abuse: hard sending gates, suppression enforcement, compliance checkboxes, bounce monitoring, and no-spam policy.

safety.title: Hard gates between collection and sending.
safety.sub: Every design decision in this platform was made with one goal: prevent messages from going out without informed operator intent. Here is exactly how that works.

sections.p: Before a single outgoing message can be queued, all five gates must pass simultaneously:
items: Sending domain DNS-verified (SPF + DKIM + DMARC + Return-Path all passing)
SMTP status = ready (platform tests connectivity before every campaign run)
Target contact status = subscribed (manually set by operator — never automatic)
Draft status = approved (manually reviewed and confirmed by operator)
No global suppression hit (checked per address before each message)

sections.p: The Collector is completely isolated from the sending pipeline. It has no SMTP code, no send queue access, and no ability to trigger messages. Collected contacts land in the Warehouse — they do not auto-flow to the sending queue under any condition.

Every imported or discovered contact arrives in 'pending' status. Pending contacts cannot receive campaign messages, test sends, or invite link notifications. Only a manual operator action moves a contact from pending to subscribed.

When a contact unsubscribes (via the one-click link in any message), their address is added to the global suppression list immediately. This is enforced at the worker level before each individual message. Suppressed addresses cannot be force-re-subscribed via bulk actions.

Every outgoing email includes a List-Unsubscribe header and a visible unsubscribe link. Both trigger the same suppression event. The platform implements RFC 8058 List-Unsubscribe-Post for mail clients that support it. No user action beyond one click is required.

The worker monitors bounce and complaint rates in real time. If bounce rate exceeds 2% or complaint rate exceeds 0.08%, the running campaign is automatically paused and the operator is notified. The campaign cannot be resumed without a manual override.

The draft approval form includes a compliance checkbox: 'I confirm this message is accurate, references only facts from the analyzed website, and complies with applicable laws (GDPR, CAN-SPAM, etc.).' The checkbox is not pre-ticked. The draft cannot be approved without ticking it.
The following uses are prohibited and result in immediate account suspension:
items: Sending to purchased, rented, or leaked email lists
Sending to contacts who have not been manually reviewed and activated
Sending in volumes that exceed per-tenant daily limits
Disabling or bypassing the suppression check
Using the platform to send phishing, malware, or fraudulent content
Marketing the platform's B2B base as a 'spray-and-pray' blast list

sections.p: Every approval, rejection, send, bounce, click, unsubscribe, and admin action is timestamped and stored. The audit log is accessible to super-admins and cannot be modified by regular operators.

zohoNote.title: Zoho manual bridge.
zohoNote.body: Optional zero-budget channel. Low-volume, operator-approved, one-by-one only. No bulk send, no scheduler, no mass subscribe. Sends only if the operator configures Zoho credentials and clicks send; otherwise drafts are copy/pasted manually. Negative replies are one-click suppressed. emails.cheap campaign rails are unchanged.

antispam.heading: The platform is built for legitimate B2B outreach only.
antispam.sub: Every design decision enforces a review-first model. There is no path from contact discovery to outbox without a human operator approving each step.

commitments.autoSendP: The platform has no scheduled auto-send without operator approval. Every campaign is manually triggered or manually scheduled.
commitments.purchasedP: Sending to purchased, rented, or leaked lists is prohibited and results in immediate account suspension.
commitments.unsubscribeP: One-click unsubscribe removes the address permanently. No re-add via bulk import.
commitments.auditP: Every approval, rejection, send, and admin action is timestamped and stored. Operators cannot modify the audit log.

seo.title: FAQ — Email Platform
seo.description: Frequently asked questions about Email Platform: how collecting works, what the safety gates are, SMTP setup, domain verification, and more.

faq.title: Common questions.
faq.sub: Practical answers about how the platform works, what the limits are, and what to do when something doesn't work as expected.

items.q: Is this a bulk email blaster?
items.a: No. The platform is designed for controlled, reviewed outreach — not bulk sending. Every message requires a manually approved draft, a DNS-verified domain, a configured SMTP, and a manually activated contact. There are no one-click bulk sends.

items.q: Can I send to any email I collect?
items.a: No. Collected contacts land in the Warehouse with status 'discovered'. To send to them you must: (1) promote them to Contacts, (2) manually set them to 'subscribed', (3) ensure a domain is verified and SMTP is ready. The system does not auto-activate any contact.

items.q: What sources does the collector use?
items.a: OpenStreetMap (via Overpass API, free), Tavily search API (requires API key, paid by query), and user-uploaded CSV files. The collector never accesses login-protected pages, CAPTCHA walls, or private systems.

items.q: How does the website analyzer work?
items.a: The analyzer fetches publicly reachable pages from a company's website. It reads the text content and generates: industry classification, offering summary, inferred pain points, confidence score (0–100), and detected language. It does not use screenshots or render JavaScript-only content.

Confidence is how much usable content the analyzer found on the website. A score of 80–100 means the site had clear, detailed content about the company's services. A score below 30 means the site was sparse, under construction, or blocked the crawler.

items.q: Can I generate drafts without website analysis?
items.a: No. The draft generator requires a completed website analysis. This ensures every draft is grounded in real, verifiable facts about the recipient's business — not generic templates.

Any SMTP provider that supports standard SMTP with AUTH PLAIN or AUTH LOGIN: Postmark, Amazon SES, Mailgun, SendGrid, or your own Postal instance. Set SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT, SMTP_USER, and SMTP_PASSWORD in your .env file.

items.q: Why do I need to verify my sending domain?
items.a: DNS verification (SPF + DKIM + DMARC + Return-Path) proves you control the domain you're sending from. This is required by most SMTP providers and inbox filters. Without verification, your messages will likely be rejected or marked as spam.

Their address is added to the global suppression list immediately. The platform checks this list before each outgoing message. Suppressed addresses cannot receive messages from any tenant. This action is permanent and cannot be reversed by bulk operations.

Yes. In perpetual mode (the default), the collector worker runs on a 50-second cycle. It picks up queued sources and processes them continuously. You add sources; the worker processes them without further action.

Bounce rate = hard bounces / delivered messages in the current campaign. Hard bounces (address not found, domain doesn't exist) increment the counter. Soft bounces (temporary failures) are retried before counting. Campaign auto-pauses at 2%.

Yes. Each tenant has a fully isolated workspace: separate contacts, domains, collector campaigns, sending settings, and audit logs. The super-admin can view and manage all tenants from the Admin panel.

All data is stored in a MariaDB database on the server that hosts the platform. Redis is used for session caching and the message queue. There is no external data transmission except SMTP outgoing messages and DNS verification lookups.

Yes. The full stack runs on Docker Compose. You need a server (Linux VPS), a domain, an SMTP provider, and a Tavily API key (optional, for search-based collection). See the Setup Center (/setup) for the full checklist.

seo.title: System Overview — Email Platform

systemOverview.title: How the platform is built.
systemOverview.sub: A public-safe technical overview of the platform architecture, services, and data flow.

services.p: Server-rendered operator console. Public landing pages, authenticated dashboard, all management UIs. Served at ports 13000 (internal) → 443 via nginx.
REST API handling auth, tenant management, lead warehouse, domains, campaigns, and tracking endpoints. JWT HS256 auth, Argon2id passwords, Zod validation, Pino logging.
Processes the collector pipeline, website analysis queue, outreach draft generation, and campaign sending. Reads jobs from Redis streams. Runs independently of the API.
Stores all tenants, users, contacts, collector data, warehouse companies, drafts, campaigns, domains, audit logs. Accessed only from API and Worker containers (internal network).
Session cache, collector job queue, send queue. All queues use Redis streams with consumer groups. Password-protected, internal network only.
Routes HTTPS traffic to Portal and API. Handles Cloudflare Full SSL termination. Serves static reports. Proxies Mailhog for test SMTP inspection.

items: All passwords hashed with Argon2id
Sessions: JWT HS256, 24h TTL, HttpOnly cookie
TLS on all connections (Cloudflare edge → nginx → containers)
CORS configured per origin
Auth rate limiting: 10 requests per minute per IP
SQL injection protection: parameterized queries throughout
XSS protection: Content-Type headers, no raw HTML injection
CSRF protection: SameSite cookie + Bearer token pattern
Secrets not logged: authorization headers redacted in Pino
Tenant isolation enforced at every database query

steps: Portal → API :4000 (internal network, no TLS required)
Worker → Redis (reads job queues) → processes → writes back to MariaDB
Worker → SMTP provider (external, for outgoing messages only)

sections.p: emails.cheap ("Platform", "we", "us") is an email outreach platform for B2B businesses. We operate at https://emails.cheap and https://email.clients.help. This policy describes how we collect, use, and protect personal data in connection with the Platform.

We collect: (a) Account data — email address, name, tenant/organisation name, hashed password. (b) Usage data — login timestamps, audit logs, campaign activity. (c) Lead warehouse data — publicly listed business contact information (business emails, websites, company names) sourced from OpenStreetMap, Tavily web search, and user-uploaded archives. All warehouse contacts are B2B (business email addresses of companies), not personal consumer addresses.

Account data is used to authenticate your account and provide the Platform services. Lead warehouse data is used solely to power outreach draft generation and sending features for the account that controls it. We do not sell, share, or trade personal data with third parties for advertising purposes.

Account data is retained while your account is active and for 30 days after deletion. Lead warehouse data is retained as long as your account is active. You may request deletion at any time by contacting support@emails.cheap.

The Platform enforces strict anti-spam controls: (a) One-click permanent unsubscribe is enforced on all outgoing emails. (b) Global suppression lists are maintained and honoured. (c) Accounts sending to purchased, leaked, or non-consenting lists are immediately suspended. (d) Sending requires SPF, DKIM, and DMARC authentication on verified domains.

The Platform uses a session cookie (token) to maintain your authenticated session. No third-party tracking, analytics, or advertising cookies are set. Email open/click tracking is implemented via signed tokens — recipients can opt out by unsubscribing.

You have the right to access, correct, or delete your personal data. You have the right to data portability and to restrict processing. To exercise these rights, contact support@emails.cheap. We respond within 30 days.

Passwords are hashed with Argon2id. All connections use TLS. Database credentials are isolated per-service. We conduct periodic security reviews. If a breach affects your data, we will notify you within 72 hours.
Privacy inquiries: support@emails.cheap
By creating an account on emails.cheap ("Platform"), you agree to these Terms. If you do not agree, do not use the Platform.

The Platform is for legitimate B2B outreach to businesses that may have a genuine interest in your product or service. You may use it to: collect publicly listed business leads, generate personalised outreach drafts with human approval, and send emails to opted-in contacts or niche-segmented business lists.

You must NOT: (a) send to purchased, harvested, leaked, or consumer email lists; (b) send spam, phishing, malware, or deceptive content; (c) impersonate other entities or falsify sender information; (d) attempt to bypass suppression, unsubscribe, or bounce handling; (e) rotate sending domains to evade spam filters; (f) use the Platform for illegal activities. Violation results in immediate account suspension.

You must: include a valid physical address in every email; provide a one-click unsubscribe link (enforced by the Platform); honour all unsubscribe and opt-out requests immediately; maintain bounce and complaint rates below industry thresholds (2% bounce, 0.08% complaint). The Platform monitors these metrics and may automatically suspend your account if thresholds are exceeded.
Approved outreach drafts must be accurate and not misleading. Claims about your product must be truthful. The Platform may review and decline content that violates these standards.

We may suspend or terminate your account immediately for: sending spam, exceeding abuse thresholds, violating these Terms, or activity that harms the Platform's IP reputation. Suspended accounts may not access their data until the matter is resolved.

mailboxesPage.flow: Add provider profile → Add mailbox → Put env vars in .env → Restart api+worker → Test SMTP/IMAP → Activate
mailboxesPage.introTail: . Secrets live in .env only — never shown here. No real emails are sent from this page.
mailboxesPage.assignDesc: Distribute queued items across healthy mailboxes (healthiest-first). Dry-run only — sets nothing.
mailboxesPage.defaultsNote1: New cold mailbox defaults to 5/day · 2/hour, status
mailboxesPage.envTitle: .env snippet (empty values only — fill with real secrets, then restart)
mailboxesPage.deleteConfirm: Delete mailbox {email}? Its stored credentials are erased. This cannot be undone.
mailboxesPage.csvTitle: CSV import / export (metadata only — never secrets)
mailboxesPage.csvCols: Columns: email, display_name, provider_profile_name|provider_profile_id, purpose, daily_send_limit, hourly_send_limit, outbound_enabled, inbound_enabled, smtp_user_ref, smtp_secret_ref, imap_user_ref, imap_secret_ref. Imported mailboxes stay draft until tested + activated.
mailboxesPage.provDesc: Shared SMTP/IMAP host+port reused by many mailboxes. Secrets are NOT stored here.
mailboxesPage.envHow: These are env-var NAMES, not values. Secrets are never saved in the browser or database. Put them in the server file /opt/email/.env (fill the part after each =), then restart: docker compose up -d api worker. After that the SMTP/IMAP test will pass and you can Activate.
mailboxesPage.credsHelp: Entered here, encrypted in the database — no .env editing needed. Secrets are write-only (never shown back). For Zoho use an app-specific password.
mailboxesPage.credsSaved: Credentials saved (encrypted). Now Test SMTP / IMAP, then Activate.
mailboxesPage.limitHint: You set the number. Recommended warmup for a new mailbox: 5/day day 1, then ramp.
mailboxesPage.credsFirst: Mailbox created. Now enter login + password below (🔑) — no .env editing.
mailboxesPage.envAdvNote: Advanced/optional: server .env setup. You normally do NOT need this — use 🔑 Credentials instead.
mailboxesPage.provAddAny: You can add ANY provider here — Gmail, Outlook/Microsoft 365, your own SMTP. Click a preset or fill the form below.
mailboxesPage.presetHint: Preset fills host/port below. Then click Create. Per-mailbox login/password are entered later with the 🔑 button (encrypted, no .env).
mailboxesPage.presetFillForm: Form filled below — set a name and click Create.
